title: Today in one sentence
text: Before the open on Thursday, Lockheed Martin has just reported its quarterly results and Meta reported last night, so those two stocks are the ones to watch when trading starts at 9:30 a.m. Eastern.

title: Meta reported after the close
text: Meta shared its third quarter results on Wednesday evening. Reports say sales were about $64.6 billion, up 26% from a year ago, but a large one-time legal charge cut its profit. The stock closed at $697.52 before the news, so today's first trades will show how investors feel about it.

title: Lockheed Martin results are out
text: Lockheed Martin reported this morning that sales rose 11% to about $20.7 billion and that its backlog (orders not yet delivered) hit a record $292 billion. The stock closed at $551.51, just under the $554 low end of analyst price targets, so watch whether it moves toward that range.

title: The 10 year bond rate is climbing
text: The 10 year Treasury yield is the interest the US government pays to borrow for ten years. Its monthly average rose to 4.99% in September, the highest of the past 12 months. When safe bonds pay more, some investors find stocks less exciting, so tech stocks can feel it.

title: Big gap in the AI group
text: Yesterday the chip makers AMD (up 3.4%) and Nvidia (up 2.5%) rose, while Alphabet fell 1.6% and Intuitive Surgical fell 2.3%. Prices can swing a lot in one day, which is why spreading money across many companies matters.

title: Lesson 18: What is free cash flow?
text: Free cash flow is the money a company has left after paying its bills and its big spending on things like factories and computers. Think of a lemonade stand: sales minus lemons, cups and a new table is what you can really keep. A company with lots of free cash flow can pay dividends, buy back shares or save for hard times. A company that spends more than it earns for a while can still be fine if the spending builds something valuable, but it is something to watch. This is for learning, not advice to buy or sell anything.
